slides.title: 12 approvers won't make a [better homepage.]
slides.lede: A 12-partner firm could have 12 people wanting to approve the homepage. That doesn't make it 12 times better. It creates a decision-making problem.

items.title: What should they do next?
items.text: The enquiry the website should encourage.

slides.title: Record four things for [every page]
slides.note: If two pages serve the same audience and answer the same question, **consider combining them.**

slides.title: Agree who [writes, approves and updates] each page
slides.text: A designer can't plan a case-study layout when no one has agreed whether the firm can supply case studies. Decide content owners before design starts.

slides.title: Get [ownership] in writing before you sign
slides.note: Ask every agency what happens if the relationship ends, and **whether the site can move to another provider.**

slides.title: Send the agency [one set] of revisions

cards.label: How projects stall
cards.text: Conflicting comments from six partners sent straight to the designers.

cards.label: How the brief prevents it
cards.text: One person consolidates feedback at each approval milestone.

slides.title: Agree what your website must prove. Then write the brief.
